- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially early in the horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history; cap forecast growth to 1–2% per day post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model fails to correct; add a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day if sentiment <0.4 for 2+ consecutive days.
